summary: This is a careful, preregistered paired evaluation asking whether embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces security-increasing (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations for an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline. Execution and archival evidence are complete and consistent: preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode validator traces, model configuration, raw results, and analysis artifacts are present. The confirmatory outcome is degenerate (no violations observed in either arm across N=300 pairs), which the authors acknowledge and interpret conservatively. The study is reproducible from the archived artifacts and the Disclosure Statement meets the track requirements. I recommend revision to improve clarity and emphasize the inferential limits imposed by the preregistered contract (shared_initial_candidate semantics) and the degenerate outcome; these are correctable from the supplied artifacts and do not require new experiments.
required_revisions: Explicitly and prominently state (in the Abstract and Methods paragraph) that the primary paired comparison used the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (single initial LLM candidate reused/persisted for both baseline and guarded playback), and that the baseline is therefore not an independent-generation condition — explain succinctly how this contract reduces the probability of observing discordant violating outputs and thus limits the confirmatory test's ability to evaluate repair efficacy. Cite the archived execution/model_configuration.json and provider-call audit in the execution manifest when making this point.

Add one short paragraph in Methods or Results that quantifies the practical consequence of the degenerate contingency table for the planned hypothesis test (i.e., explicitly state that with n11=300 and n10=n01=0 the McNemar test is uninformative for repair efficacy), and point readers to the archived one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound (analysis artifact) as the appropriate post-hoc descriptive bound. Include the numeric bound (≈0.00994) inline and cite analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv or analysis/condition_summary.csv. This change is editorial and can be implemented from archived analysis artifacts.

Clarify in Methods and Disclosure exactly how the two validators were combined into the decision rule used during scoring (logical OR, AND, thresholding, tie-breaking) — although the manuscript states a logical OR, make this explicit in the scoring subsection and reference the per-episode validator_trace fields in the archived scoring artifacts for verification (execution/scoring/*.json).
optional_revisions: Include a concise nearest-work comparison table or a short paragraph explicitly comparing the study design and experimental contract choices to the closest prior GVR/NetOps verifier-in-the-loop demonstrations (cite the verified bibliography entries), to help readers assess where the current evidence fits relative to prior art.

Provide a short appendix sentence pointing to the exact Batfish container-image tags/digests and the Python static-analyzer file SHA-256 (already archived in execution/execution_manifest.json) and explicitly name the validator components (Batfish + static analyzer) in the Disclosure rather than only logical identifiers, to further ease reproduction.

Discuss briefly (one paragraph) how the shared_initial_candidate contract was chosen (trade-offs between model-call budget and inferential power) and include a short recommendation (with artifact pointers) for a follow-up experimental contract (e.g., independent-condition draws or expanded repair budgets) that would exercise the repair path.
